title: GAIE Endpoint Picker: priority-aware admission, flow control and endpoint placement for LLM inference
source: kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension @ 2711ff86a50ae23c5d32387779df8d3db9ca28e4 (cloned HEAD). pkg/epp was deleted in a70292c, so all evidence is read and re-verified at a70292c^ = 1748e829d1161147aaf35e76699ec86fd88406d2
purpose: A proxy sidecar that admits, queues and places each inference request on exactly one model-server pod of a shared pool using pluggable filters, weighted scorers and a fairness-aware priority queue.

interface.entry: a gRPC external-processing stream handed to the director (pkg/epp/handlers/server.go:162, :326)
interface.request: an OpenAI-shaped body plus headers carrying an objective key, an optional x-slo-ttft-ms deadline, and an endpoint-subset metadata filter (pkg/epp/requestcontrol/director.go:173)
interface.response: mutated body plus an x-gateway-destination-endpoint value, or a typed error rendered as 400/401/403/404/429/500/503 (pkg/common/error/error.go:62)
interface.config: an EndpointPickerConfig YAML plus about 35 flags, with a default injected for any plugin role left empty (pkg/epp/server/options.go:120, pkg/epp/config/loader/defaults.go:123)

model_selection.property: The model named in the body is served unchanged unless an operator-declared rewrite rule matches its name, in which case one target is drawn at random in proportion to declared integer weights and written back into the body.
model_selection.guarantee: Guarantees the served model is either the requested one or a declared rewrite target; refuses any quality- or price-based substitution, and with equal weights (or a total weight of zero) the draw is uniform and not reproducible.

placement.property: Every candidate endpoint passes a filter chain, then accumulates a weighted sum of scorer outputs each clamped into the unit interval, and the picker returns the highest-scoring endpoint with random tie-breaking.
placement.guarantee: Guarantees exactly one endpoint by default, drawn from the surviving candidates; refuses to guarantee determinism, because ties are broken by a wall-clock-seeded shuffle. Shipped weights: queue depth 2.0, memory pressure 2.0, prefix locality 3.0, unweighted scorers 1.0.

admission_and_overload.property: Admission is decided BEFORE endpoints are located. The legacy controller refuses a request only if its priority is negative and mean pool saturation is at least 1.0; the flow-control controller instead blocks the caller in a per-workload bounded queue and returns a typed outcome.
admission_and_overload.guarantee: Guarantees that a request with non-negative priority is never refused for load on the legacy path, and that every queued request ends in exactly one terminal outcome visible to the caller: dispatched, capacity-rejected (429), deadline-expired (503) or client-cancelled (503). Saturation is the mean over candidates of max(waiting/5, memory/0.8); a stale or metric-less endpoint contributes a full 1.0. Per-band queue capacity is 1 GB; the global byte and request caps default to unlimited, and the documented 5000-request per-band cap is never applied.

rate_limit_pacing.property: not decided: there is no request or token quota accounting of any kind. The only headroom signal is live endpoint utilisation, converted into a dispatch ceiling per priority band.
rate_limit_pacing.guarantee: Refuses to guarantee anything about an upstream's published allowance. The nearest analogue is a per-endpoint ideal-capacity figure and a static usage ceiling that defaults to 1.0, meaning dispatch stops only at complete saturation, leaving no reserve.

retry_and_fallback.property: not decided at the request level. A scheduling or admission failure is returned to the caller immediately; there is no second attempt, no fallback endpoint and no back-off schedule anywhere.
retry_and_fallback.guarantee: Guarantees a single placement attempt per request and an explicit typed error on failure; refuses any retry or fallback, with the source carrying an open note acknowledging the gap. The only loop in the system re-places a request whose chosen shard began draining, after a short randomised pause.

outage_and_health.property: Endpoint health is inferred purely from telemetry freshness. The candidate set is every pod in the datastore; no error counting, quarantine or timed re-probe exists.
outage_and_health.guarantee: Guarantees that an endpoint whose state is older than 200 ms is scored as fully saturated and dropped from routing; refuses to guarantee exclusion when EVERY endpoint is stale, because the filter then returns the unfiltered list and knowingly routes into the dark. State refreshes every 50 ms; a separate 2 s staleness flag affects only the metric logger, not placement.

deadline_and_priority.property: Each request carries one integer priority from its workload objective (default 0, negative means expendable). Priority bands are dispatched strictly highest-first; within a workload the ordering policy decides, defaulting to arrival order, with an optional deadline ordering keyed on the request's declared time-to-first-token budget.
deadline_and_priority.guarantee: Guarantees strict priority-band ordering and head-of-line blocking: if the selected band is saturated the whole dispatch cycle stops rather than letting lower-priority work proceed. Under the deadline policy a request with no or malformed declared budget is assigned a far-future deadline and sorts last. A request's remaining deadline becomes its queue time to live, whose default is 0 meaning no limit, swept every 1 s.

tenant_isolation.property: Work is partitioned into flows keyed by caller identity and priority; each flow gets its own queue inside its priority band, and a fairness policy chooses which flow's queue to serve next.
tenant_isolation.guarantee: Guarantees only a shared byte budget per band (1 GB) and load spreading across shards by shortest-queue-by-bytes; refuses starvation-freedom by default, because the SHIPPED fairness policy ignores flow boundaries entirely and always takes the globally best pending item, so one workload can monopolise a band. Starvation-freedom requires explicitly selecting the rotating policy. Idle flows are reclaimed after 5 minutes, bands after 10.

policy_state_and_determinism.property: The policy carries substantial cross-request state (a prefix-locality table per server, per-band rotation cursors, live endpoint telemetry, per-workload queues) and draws on a process-wide random source seeded from the wall clock.
policy_state_and_determinism.guarantee: Refuses reproducibility: identical inputs can yield different endpoints, because the source is seeded from the current time and the picker shuffles before a stable sort. Bounds memory explicitly: the prefix table is capped at 31250 blocks per server with at most 256 blocks matched at 16 tokens each, inactive pods are swept every 2 minutes, idle flows reclaimed after 5 minutes, and the per-request response queue is capped at 100 chunks.

cost_control.property: not decided: spend is bounded by nothing. There is no price table, per-request cost estimate, budget or spend counter anywhere.
cost_control.guarantee: Refuses any spend guarantee. The only bounded resources are queued bytes per priority band and per-endpoint utilisation thresholds; price never enters a scoring or admission decision.

decision_observability.property: Every request opens a trace span tagged with target model and priority, logs the chosen endpoint and each plugin's verdict, and increments per-stage metrics; every refusal is returned to the caller as a typed error with a status and a human-readable cause.
decision_observability.guarantee: Guarantees that a refusal is visible to the caller WITH its cause (resource exhausted, timed out in queue, client disconnected, internal error) and that per-plugin latency, scheduling attempts, queue size, queued bytes and pool saturation are all exported. Refuses to surface enrichment failures: they are logged and the request proceeds on degraded information, indistinguishable to the caller from a fully informed decision.
